title: Covered pedestrian concourse with '香港大學站 HKU Station' sign and HKU-branded queue belts
objects_and_counts: One person is partially visible and cropped at the far left edge of the image (left torso and arm visible only).
At least nine vertical structural columns or posts are visible along the left and right sides of the concourse (several are partially obscured by perspective).

Three small wooden-topped stands or tables are visible in the foreground: one at the left edge (cropped), one roughly centered near a stanchion, and one at the right side next to a small upright sign on a stand.
Two green retractable belt stanchion posts are visible forming a short queue or barrier in the foreground; the belts are printed with 'HKU' repeated along them.
One freestanding sign on a metal stand is visible mounted on the right wooden-topped table (text on the signboard is partially legible; see visible_text and uncertainties).
One large hanging overhead station sign is visible centered in the image reading '香港大學站 HKU Station'.
Multiple glass panels and metal railings line the right side of the concourse; a glazed building façade is visible outside on the right.
Multiple overhead ceiling panels and linear light fixtures are visible across the ceiling of the concourse.
A distant doorway or gated opening is visible at the far end of the corridor with additional small directional signs above it (symbols present; text described in visible_text where legible).
spatial_relations: The large '香港大學站 HKU Station' hanging sign is centered above the walkway, roughly mid-image horizontally and nearer the far end of the corridor.
The walkway runs from the foreground to a distant opening at the center of the image; the camera viewpoint is on the walkway facing that opening.
Vertical columns are placed along both sides of the walkway; low metal-and-glass balustrades run between them on the right side and a raised ledge with glazing runs on the left side.
Two retractable-belt stanchions are positioned across the foreground walkway forming a short barrier; a small wooden-topped stand with a sign is immediately to the right of that barrier.
The glazed multi-storey building exterior is adjacent to and visible through the right-side balustrade, occupying the rightmost portion of the image.
The partial person is standing at the extreme left edge of the image, next to the left-most wooden-topped stand which is against the left balustrade.
colours_and_materials: Ceiling panels are light grey or off-white and arranged in long horizontal strips.
Structural columns and metal railings are painted or finished in a grey/blue-grey metal colour.
Flooring is composed of large grey concrete or stone tiles with a darker textured central strip running down the walkway.
The hanging station sign has a dark blue background with white and red elements for the logo and white text.
The retractable belts are green with white 'HKU' lettering; the wooden-topped stands have medium-brown wood-coloured tops and darker metal legs.
The building façade visible on the right is predominantly light blue/teal glass with visible external metal bracing in a blue tone.
uncertainties: Smaller text on the freestanding sign on the right wooden-topped table is only partly legible in the image; the exact wording and Chinese characters cannot be fully transcribed from this resolution.
There are additional small directional signs and symbols above the distant doorway; some pictograms are visible but accompanying text is too small or distant to read accurately.

The exact count of vertical columns may be higher than the stated 'at least nine' because some columns are partly obscured by perspective or by other elements; I report only those individually distinguishable in this view.
The partial person at the left edge is cropped and cannot be more fully described; no identifying information is provided or inferred.
The repeated instances of 'HKU' on the belts are transcribed as a repeated visible element but each occurrence beyond those listed may be present out of frame or on other belts not fully visible.
